method: At a steady speed v, a clock moving with the traveller ticks slower than one left behind by the Lorentz factor gamma = 1 / sqrt(1 - v squared / c squared), so a trip of D light-years takes D / v years on Earth and D / (v gamma) years on board, while the crew measures the distance as D / gamma. The page takes the speed as a percentage of c and the distance in light-years, and computes gamma from (1 - b)(1 + b) rather than 1 - b squared so that speeds very close to c keep their significant digits instead of cancelling them. It reports the traveller's elapsed time, the Earth-frame time, the shortened distance measured on board and the speed in km/s, or in m/s below walking pace. Times and distances carry six significant digits and a value rounded to 1 prints as a singular year. The model is the special-relativity result for constant velocity: it ignores the acceleration at departure and arrival and any gravitational time dilation, so it is an illustration rather than a flight plan. Speeds above 0 and below 100% of c are accepted with a distance above 0 light-years; 100% of c and beyond is refused because no object with mass reaches it. Everything runs in the browser; nothing is uploaded, stored or sent anywhere.
